description: Log-normal distribution cumulative distribution function Phi((ln x - mu) / sigma) (location mu, scale sigma)

tolerance.reason: x is an exact double but ln x is not: rounding ln x costs |ln x| 2^-53 in w = (ln x - mu) / sigma after dividing by sigma, and rounding w costs |w| 2^-53. Phi's condition number in w, phi(w) / Phi(w), is about |w| in the lower tail, so a method that rounds ln x and w loses (|ln x| / sigma + |w|) phi(w) / Phi(w) 2^-53, at most 3.4e-13 at a normal result on this grid (mu = -3, sigma = 0.5, w = -37.5); 8e-13 is 2.35x that, the margin norm_cdf keeps (4e-13 over its 1.6e-13: 2.5x) for roundings of up to an ulp rather than half an ulp. SciPy flushes the subnormal result at w = -38 to 0. Results below 2.2e-308 are judged relative to that number (conventions)

grid: (mu, sigma) in {(0, 0.25), (-3, 0.5), (0, 1), (2, 4)} x x = the double nearest exp(mu + sigma w) for w = -40..40 step 0.5, plus x = 0 and x = -1; F is 0 for x <= 0, subnormal from about w = -37.52, 0 below about w = -38.49 and rounds to 1 above about w = 8.3
